brief: Verdict ahead of the print: the quarter itself should look flat sequentially, at about $1.07bn of revenue against $1,065.4mn in 2Q26. The stock will trade on three things: whether the FY26 guide holds near the top, whether Jupiter's delays move any shipments, and whether management gives a number that supports the 63% revenue growth the market expects for FY27.

Where expectations sit. Yahoo Finance shows 3Q26 revenue consensus of $1.07bn from 16 analysts (range $909.9mn to $1.13bn) and non-GAAP EPS of $0.67 from 17 analysts. Zacks has $0.71, and MarketBeat, Benzinga and TipRanks fall between $0.68 and $0.69. FY26 consensus is $4.12bn and $2.71, near the top of the raised $3.9bn to $4.2bn and $2.55 to $2.85 guide. FY27 consensus is $6.71bn and $4.94. Taking H1 revenue of $1,816.4mn and a 3Q of $1.07bn, the market expects about $1.2bn in 4Q.

What the quarter should show. Bloom said in July that what used to be seasonality is now delivery timing set by customer readiness, and that 2026 does not depend on any single project. 2Q26 non-GAAP gross margin was 34.3%, which included a $37.4mn tariff recovery; without it, margin was 30.8%. Reaching the FY margin of about 34% needs about 34.7% in the second half. Operating cash flow was $300.0mn in H1, and the CFO calls '$375 million plus' the new baseline.

Three debates. First, Jupiter. Oracle's New Mexico campus is meant to run entirely on Bloom fuel cells, but the gas pipeline has slipped to February 2027, the air-permit hearing is on 7 December, and microgrid construction has not begun. Enverus, cited by TIKR, puts Jupiter at nearly half of Bloom's backlog; this is unverified. Second, margin quality: one-off tariff recoveries, the $58.3mn specific warranty reserve, and one customer at 73% of 2Q26 revenue. Third, the FY27 bridge: Bloom publishes no backlog figure, and 10-Q RPO is only $442.4mn.

What would move the stock. Positive: the guide raised or held at the top, a firm Jupiter delivery schedule that does not depend on the permit, a disclosed order book or capacity plan in GW, and gross margin of 34% or more without recoveries. Negative: any 2026 revenue moved into 2027, margin below 33% on a clean basis, or a weak cash quarter with rising receivables. The stock closed at $238.53 on 21 October and traded at $225.34 at 9:54 am ET on 22 October. Options imply a move of about 10%.

Kona read-through. Jupiter shows that at gigawatt scale, behind-the-meter gas power is limited by pipeline gas and air permits, not by the equipment. Kona's wellhead gas in Vaca Muerta is an advantage, but only if it is backed by firm gas contracts and an emissions permit before a tenant signs.
changes: Since the July print, Project Jupiter (Oracle, up to 2.45 GW of Bloom fuel cells) has slipped on infrastructure. Transwestern's gas pipeline moved to February 2027, Oracle served a force majeure notice on 24 September, and the air-permit hearing moved to 7 December with a proposed output cap.

New named demand: AEP will build a 702 MW, $4bn Bloom fuel-cell plant in Cheyenne for Google under a 20-year PPA (14 October), and Bloom will power Aligned's 2 GW Project Phoenix in Pennsylvania (September).

Consensus has settled at the top of the raised guide: FY26 revenue of $4.12bn against $3.9bn to $4.2bn, and FY26 EPS of $2.71 against $2.55 to $2.85. 3Q26 revenue consensus of $1.07bn is roughly flat on 2Q26.
The stock fell 21% in the week to 16 October and now sits about 32% below its 25 June high, despite S&P 500 inclusion on 21 September.
The 2Q26 margin beat was flattered by a $37.4mn tariff recovery, partly offset by a $58.3mn specific warranty reserve, so the second-half margin run-rate is now an open question.
checks: No subagent was available, so I verified the figures myself. Filing figures: I downloaded the 2Q26 release, 10-Q, 10-Q/A and 8-K of 9 July from EDGAR, converted them to text, and string-matched 73 figures against the saved text in code (revenue lines, margins, non-GAAP operating income, EBITDA, EPS, OCF, cash, receivables, contract assets, deposits, warranty, RPO, debt table, conversion terms, letter-of-credit line, performance guarantees, Oracle warrant, concentration, share count). All matched; the $37.4mn tariff recovery matched after normalizing a line break. 3Q25 revenue of $519.0mn was confirmed in SEC XBRL company facts. FY25 revenue of $2,024.0mn and the FY26 guide were read from slide images in the 2Q26 supplement. Customer concentration uses the 10-Q/A, which swapped the original 10-Q's three-month and six-month labels: 73% is one customer's share of 2Q26 revenue. Consensus: Yahoo and StockAnalysis pages were saved on 22 October and string-matched (counts, averages, ranges, EPS trend, targets, ratings, price history). I reopened the Zacks/Yahoo, POWER, Stocktwits, ENR and MGRID articles and confirmed each figure used, quoted from the page. TipRanks, Benzinga, Schaeffer's, MarketBeat, TIKR and Invezz were each read once. Derived numbers were recomputed in Python: H1 totals, second-half needs, implied 4Q, margin without the tariff recovery, second-half margin needed, net cash, market cap, multiples, conversion shares, $/kW, and the price moves. TipRanks's $25.39 implied move differs slightly from 10.7% of the 20 October close ($23.82). Not verified or single source: the Oracle 2.8 GW MSA and 1.2 GW contracted (Stocktwits); the Brookfield $6.4bn package for Meta, American Tower, Equinix and CoreWeave (BMO via Timothy Sykes); Jupiter as nearly half of backlog (Enverus via TIKR); the CFO's 'financier is on the hook' wording (quoted by TIKR; the Investing.com transcript gives a similar redeploy answer); the Hunterbrook accounting claims (only Bloom's denial and press summaries were read). No convertible price, yield or CDS was found for 21 or 22 October. No quarterly consensus was found for gross margin, operating income or EBITDA, and Bloom publishes no backlog figure. The 22 October price ($225.34) is intraday at 9:54 am ET. The 3Q26 release had not been filed when this card was built (latest EDGAR filing checked: 2 October), and no post-results material was read. Independent subagent verifier re-downloaded EDGAR filings and market pages on 22 Oct 2026 and confirmed all filing and consensus figures; call quotes and Jupiter items remain unconfirmed by primary source.
consensus_thesis: Investors own Bloom as the default supplier of fast, on-site, non-combustion power for AI data centers, and at about $70bn (about 48x FY27 consensus EPS) they are paying for revenue doubling to about $4.1bn in FY26 and rising 63% to about $6.7bn in FY27 at mid-30s margins; positioning is contested after a short report and the Jupiter scare, and the in-the-money 0% 2030 convertibles carry no separate credit signal.
headline: 3Q26 is judged less on a roughly flat $1.07bn quarter than on whether Bloom can show that the second-half ramp, margins and the 2027 order book hold up while Oracle's Project Jupiter waits for a gas pipeline and an air permit.
kona: Jupiter shows that behind-the-meter gas power at scale is held up by the pipeline and the air permit, not the equipment. Even non-combustion fuel cells drew a contested permit hearing and a proposed output cap. Kona's wellhead gas in Vaca Muerta is a real advantage over a site waiting for a pipeline, but tenants and lenders will want a firm gas supply agreement and an emissions permit in hand before they sign. If Kona sells power, Bloom's structures are the template to test: a financier owns modular, redeployable equipment and sells power under a PPA (Brookfield, IDF), at all-in costs near AEP's Cheyenne plant (about $5,700/kW by our arithmetic, including more than the fuel cells).

name: Bloom Energy

questions.question: In July you said the 2026 guide 'is not dependent on any single project' and that the financier 'is on the hook to take delivery.' Since then Transwestern's pipeline has moved to February 2027, the air-permit hearing has moved to 7 December, and microgrid construction has not started. You also carry a $306.5mn Oracle customer-consideration asset that amortizes only as Oracle systems are delivered. How many MW of Oracle or Jupiter systems were in 3Q26 revenue, and how many are in the 4Q guide? Is any of it contingent on the permit? If the permit slips into 2027, does the financier still take title and pay in 2026, yes or no?
questions.why: Jupiter is the largest named project, and Enverus puts it at nearly half the backlog (unverified). If revenue recognition depends on the permit, the FY26 guide and the FY27 bridge carry a regulatory risk that the multiple does not price.

questions.question: 2Q26 non-GAAP gross margin was 34.3%, but 30.8% without the $37.4mn tariff recovery, and in the same quarter you booked a $58.3mn specific warranty reserve. Your FY guide of about 34% needs about 34.7% in the second half. What was 3Q gross margin excluding recoveries and specific reserves? Which fleet or component does the reserve cover? Should we expect more specific reserves as the data center fleet ages?
questions.why: The valuation assumes mid-30s margins on a doubling revenue base. A clean run-rate near 31%, or a fleet-wide warranty issue, would cut FY27 EPS and add a liability that grows with the installed base.

questions.question: H1 operating cash flow was $300.0mn against your '$375mn plus' baseline. At 30 June, three customers held 87% of receivables, contract assets had doubled to $365.5mn, and one customer was 73% of 2Q revenue. What share of receivables and contract assets at 30 September is owed by financing vehicles (Brookfield JVs, IDF) rather than investment-grade end users? Is any collection conditional on a project financing closing? Will you commit to a FY26 operating cash flow figure?
questions.why: Bloom's credit depends on collecting from a few counterparties, some of them financing vehicles. If profit sits in receivables and contract assets rather than cash, that is the early sign of a funding need.

questions.question: You have $2.5bn of 0% notes due 2030, convertible at $194.97 (about 12.8mn shares), about $137mn of net cash, and a letter-of-credit line that was fully used at 30 June, while analysts model capacity of 6 to 10 GW a year. What is 2027 factory capex, and how will it be funded? Are customers asking for more letters of credit or performance bonds as project size grows? Do you intend to settle any conversion of the 2030 notes in cash or in shares?
questions.why: Net cash is thin relative to the growth plan. Settlement policy and bonding needs determine whether growth is funded internally or by dilution and secured debt.

questions.question: Consensus FY27 revenue is $6.71bn, up 63%, yet the 10-Q shows only $442.4mn of product and installation RPO, and you have not published a backlog figure. What GW and dollar value of firm orders with deposits is scheduled for 2027 delivery, and what share comes from your top three customers? If you will not give a number, will you confirm whether signed orders cover more or less than half of FY27 consensus?
questions.why: The share price rests on FY27. Without disclosed firm orders, the market is valuing announcements such as Jupiter, Cheyenne and Phoenix that may convert to revenue later than modelled.

risks: Project Jupiter delays (pipeline, air permit, emissions cap) push Bloom shipments or revenue recognition into 2027.
Margin quality: one-off tariff recoveries and specific warranty reserves hide the underlying run-rate.
Customer concentration: one customer was 73% of 2Q26 revenue, and three customers held 87% of receivables.
Short-seller allegations (Hunterbrook, July 2026) on accounting and scandium sourcing, plus the related class actions.
Valuation risk: about 48x FY27 EPS, with a wide FY27 revenue range of $5.3bn to $8.26bn; data center opposition and moratoria (New York).

sections.body: Bloom makes solid-oxide fuel cells, run mainly on pipeline natural gas, and sells them per kW as islanded on-site power for AI data centers. The buyer is either the end user or a financing vehicle (the Brookfield JVs under a $25bn framework, or IDF at $2.6bn) that owns the equipment and sells power under a PPA. Product was 88% of 2Q26 revenue. Service contracts and legacy electricity sales add recurring revenue. Bloom's own capital needs are small (factory capex and working capital), and it is funded by cash and $2.5bn of 0% convertible notes due 2030.

sections.body: 1) Jupiter: do the pipeline and permit delays move Bloom revenue out of 2026, and how much of the backlog is one Oracle campus? 2) Margin quality: can non-GAAP gross margin stay at or above 34% without tariff recoveries, and is the $58.3mn specific warranty reserve a one-off? 3) The FY27 bridge: is the 63% growth in consensus backed by firm orders and capacity, and will Bloom disclose backlog in GW and $?
sections.title: Live debates

sections.body: 3Q26 EPS consensus runs from $0.67 (Yahoo) to $0.71 (Zacks), and revenue from $1.05bn (Benzinga) to $1.07bn. Average price targets range from $257.18 (MarketBeat, 14 October) through $285.43 (S&P Global) to $296.72 (TipRanks). TipRanks also gives the wrong year-ago revenue ($826.13mn); EDGAR shows $519.0mn. On Jupiter, Oracle says the project is on schedule and the force majeure notice does not establish a delay, while filings cited by ENR list microgrid completion in November 2029. On capacity, the 2 GW figure came from an analyst's question, and Baird models 6 to 10 GW; management has confirmed neither. On the stock, Truist, BMO and Roth (Hold, $240 to $260) differ from Baird, Mizuho and UBS ($350 to $351).

sections.body: At 30 June 2026: cash of $2,666.9mn plus $21.6mn restricted; recourse debt principal of $2,527.8mn (total debt principal $2,530.3mn including a $2.6mn non-recourse Korean JV loan), of which $2,500.0mn is 0% notes due November 2030, convertible at $194.97 (about 12.8mn shares at the base rate); $27.0mn of 3% Green Notes due 2029 remain, and the last $0.8mn of 2028 notes was redeemed on 10 July. Nothing is drawn on the $600mn revolver, but the $90mn letter-of-credit sub-facility is fully used, leaving $510mn available. Deferred revenue and deposits total $445.0mn. Capped fleet performance guarantees total $846.1mn, with $468.9mn of remaining potential payments. We found no market price for the convertibles on 21 or 22 October.
